integration_decision.finding: Prior orphan pre-cleanup contract requires TimeoutError but does not prove which call raised it. At pinned runner.py:120 append_observations runs before runner.py:121 load_observations; storage.py:136-142 bypasses writer lock on empty input, while storage.py:97-100 always locks the reader. Both paths use ArchiveWriterLock.__enter__ and the same TimeoutError message. A bounded child deadline of 10s is also too short for the lock's default 10s timeout (storage.py:17,30-34), causing a timing false negative.
integration_decision.runnable_contract: Freeze valid PIT-visible rowB fixture; assert direct JsonlFlowAdapter.collect() yields exactly one rowB and archive/output paths are initially absent. Positively ACK owner lock acquired, crash with os._exit(17), join and verify orphan inode/owner and child exit. In separate bounded child run the exact run_once(network=False,external_jsonl=(fixture,),local_dir=tmp_path,as_of_ms=T); wait >=15s (> default lock timeout), send exception type, traceback frame/function names and elapsed time to parent; assert TimeoutError originated in append_observations -> ArchiveWriterLock.__enter__ (not load_observations), and no archive or any three outputs. Only after confirmed death remove the test-owned orphan; same run_once must report local collector OK/count1, source_errors=[], appended=1, archive/scoring=1/1, persisted/returned rowB role and source_record_id; repeat appended=0 and archive/scoring remain 1/1. Keep separate positive-ACK overlap, same-clock rollback and role identity tests. Do not use elapsed time as sole correctness oracle.
